originality.rationale: The motivating preprint makes the broader nonexpanding nonexistence assertion, but its precise theorem only treats an eigenvalue of modulus less than one. The explicit neutral family and comparison partition are not stated in the inspected primary sources, and targeted searches for the matrix model, identity-times-doubling aliases, smooth generators, neutral eigenvalues, and comparison coding returned no implication-equivalent result. The closest prior theorem is restricted to hyperbolic nonexpanding maps and generating Rokhlin partitions. Residual risk from older general generator literature and an inaccessible related HAL full text is recorded.
residual_risks: An equivalent comparison coding could exist in older general finite-generator literature that was not surfaced by the targeted searches; that would affect originality, not correctness.

value.rationale: The construction resolves the precise neutral-spectrum boundary of a fresh nonexistence assertion: it shows that replacing a strict contracting eigenvalue by mere nonexpansion is impossible even for a simple noninvertible product family with identity neutral directions and one doubling direction. The result is a structural counterexample family, not a parameter tweak, and clarifies why an expanding coordinate can encode invariant neutral coordinates through smooth comparisons.
